`common/protocolLivenessMonitor.ts` supplies the renderer and host watchdogs. Both reset on inbound traffic (including partial message data), probe application-level liveness with JSON-RPC `ping`, and defer timeouts during high local load. The renderer retains its 5-second idle probe and 25-second silence deadline, including its reverse-request deferral and reconnect behavior. Each non-local host connection probes after 10 seconds and closes after 30 seconds of inbound silence; ordinary renderer pings normally prevent host probes. Outgoing session updates alone do not prove a renderer is alive. A host timeout follows the normal transport-close path, starting the existing 30-second tool-call reconnect grace rather than replaying outstanding tools. Local MessagePort connections retain their process-owned lifetime. A peer's unsupported-method response also proves liveness, so older conforming clients need no new capability.

+Clients supplied with paired OS power events pause automatic reconnect attempts and the recovery deadline during suspension, then retry after resume with backoff while the network returns. Successful in-flight steps wait for resume before continuing; terminal authentication or protocol rejections remain authoritative during suspension. Credential acquisition failures remain retryable; explicit credential rejection or unsafe credential encryption stops recovery as an authentication failure, not a protocol-version mismatch. Protocol mismatches retain the host's supported versions and advertised upgrade method during recovery. Cloud and user-local connection-outcome telemetry records observed sleep time and bounded recovery-stop decisions without credentials or diagnostic text.

`IAgentHostPromptCache` (`node/agentHostPromptCache.ts`) exposes exactly `read(session)` / `write(session, state)` over the `vscode.promptCache` `_meta` slot. `write` re-reads the persisted value first (several live provider sessions can share one session URI), skips a no-op write, merges rather than replaces `_meta`, and returns the effective state.
